**Identity & Significance**: Ludovico Simonetta (ludovico-simonetta) was a Italian Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal born in unknown year, died on May 10, 1568. He played a crucial role in the governance of the Catholic Church during the Renaissance era.

**What Happened**: As a prominent cleric, Ludovico Simonetta participated in several key events, including the Council of Trent (1545-1563) and the Counter-Reformation. His influence extended to the appointment of numerous bishops and cardinals, shaping the ecclesiastical landscape of Italy and beyond.

**Legacy & Consequence**: The effects of Ludovico Simonetta's leadership can be seen in the enduring presence of the Catholic Church in Italy and its global reach. His legacy also influenced the development of Catholicism's dogma and doctrine during the Counter-Reformation era.

Ludovico Simonetta was a skilled diplomat who navigated complex religious politics, often walking a fine line between loyalty to the Pope and the needs of his diocese.
